shipped_row.boundary_rationale: “Behold, he spreads his light around him. He covers the bottom of the sea.” (web:Job.36.30) opens on the FOURTH הֵן within this chapter at the combined skeleton tier (segol הֶן sweep: 10 book-wide/9 verse-initial, with ch.36 members 36:5/36:22/36:26; accent-free tsere הֵן sweep: 4 verse-initial book-wide — 27:12, 33:6, 36:30, MT 41:1 — with a further 17 verse-initial tokens carrying cantillation as a separate accent-bearing sub-object; folding the segol and accent-free-tsere sub-objects into one skeleton-tier count of 4 verse-initial occurrences in ch.36 gives the ordinal “fourth”), describing lightning and the storm as the agents of judgment: “For by these he judges the people. He gives food in abundance.” (web:Job.36.31). The unit runs through the storm's noise at 36:33 and crosses the chapter number — a tier-4 boundary, not itself evidentiary — into 37:1, where the deictic אַף לְ֭זֹאת (“Yes, at this” in web:Job.37.1) ties Elihu's own bodily tremor back to the storm just narrated, closing the strophe on Elihu's own reaction rather than opening a new one. The next verse's plural imperative (שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמ֣וֹעַ, “hear, oh hear”) launches a fresh, audience-directed unit.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Starting the next row at 37:1 rather than 37:2 was considered, since a new chapter number sits there, but the chapter break is tier-4 and the deictic 'at this' in 37:1 grammatically closes the storm description rather than opening the imperative section that follows.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Lightning as judgment agent, moving from description to Elihu tremor

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A third הֶן-opening begins the unit: “Behold, God is great, and we don't know him. The number of his years is unsearchable.” (web:Job.36.26), stating וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע (“we don't know him” at web:Job.36.26). Verses 27-28 describe the water cycle — rain drawn up and poured down — and the strophe closes on a matching cognitive verb from a different root, אַ֣ף אִם יָ֭בִין מִפְרְשֵׂי עָ֑ב תְּ֝שֻׁא֗וֹת סֻכָּתֽוֹ (“Indeed, can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds and the thunderings of his pavilion?”, web:Job.36.29). The bracket is thematic rather than a shared lexical root — the opening colon’s closing verb וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע (“know”) and the verse’s closing verb (“understand”) come from two different roots — but both frame the same claim that the meteorological mechanism is beyond human grasp. The same opening-colon collocation וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע recurs in verse-final position at the skeleton tier at 37:5’s וְלֹ֣א נֵדָֽע (differing only in final accent; skeleton sweep: 4 book-wide — 8:9, 15:9, 36:26, 37:5), a skeleton-tier bracket straddling both this row’s own far seam (36:29|36:30) and the downstream 37:1|37:2 seam; disclosed here as continuity texture weighed against the strophe division rather than as a boundary override, since Elihu's fourth speech (36:1-37:24) is one continuous unit regardless of where its rows are cut. The unit closes before a fourth הֶן-opening — at the combined/skeleton tier (segol הֶן at 36:5/36:22/36:26 plus tsere הֵן at 36:30, sweep: 4 verse-initial occurrences in ch.36) — turns to lightning at 36:30.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 'we do not know' and 'can he understand' as one lexical inclusio was avoided on purpose, since the two verbs come from different roots (ידע and בין); the bracket is argued as thematic, not as root repetition.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Water cycle cosmology: divine mechanism beyond human knowing grasp

next_row.boundary_rationale: A plural imperative opens the unit: “Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.” (web:Job.37.2), the verb שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמ֣וֹעַ (‘hear, oh hear’) built on an infinitive-absolute intensifier and addressed to listeners rather than to God or Job by name -- a discourse-frame shift distinct from both the hymn's הן-openings before it and the direct 'you'-address after it. The unit describes the thunder's roar through 37:4-5, closing on “God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.” (web:Job.37.5), before the causal כִּ֤י (‘for’) opens a quotation frame at 37:6.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 37:1-5 together as one span was set aside because 37:1 is Elihu's own bodily response closing the prior unit, while 37:2's plural imperative opens a distinct audience-directed call to attention.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Call-to-attention imperative on thunder and divine voice

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Third-person description resumes without an interrogative or vocative: “Now men don’t see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.” (web:Job.37.21), moving through the golden splendor from the north (37:22) and the Almighty's inaccessibility (37:23) to the speech's closing line, “Therefore men revere him. He doesn’t regard any who are wise of heart.” (web:Job.37.24). A PE mark follows this verse in the Masoretic tradition (oshb:Job.37.24, petuchah, single-witness) -- tier-3 corroboration that sits exactly at this part's closing seam. What follows at 38:1 is a full participant and register change: a fresh vaya'an formula, וַיַּֽעַן יְהוָ֣ה (‘and he answered, Yahweh’, web:Job.38.1), opening the earliest of the three YHWH vaya'an formulas in the book (sweep: 3 book-wide, at 38:1/40:1/40:6) and the Tetragrammaton's initial speech, carrying the ketiv/qere pair מנ הסערה (ketiv) / מִ֥ן הַסְּעָרָ֗ה (qere) inside the formula (‘out of the whirlwind’) -- disclosed here since the seam argument cites it. Chapter 38 itself carries no Masoretic paragraph mark of its own, so from this side the 38:1 seam rests on the formula and the speaker change alone, with the 37:24 mark noted above as weak corroboration alongside it.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this span through 38:1 as one continuous unit was rejected outright, since 38:1 introduces an entirely new speaker, Yahweh, on its own verse-initial formula -- a participant change, not a continuation.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Third-person closure: men revere him, speech ends with PE mark

prev_row.boundary_rationale: Elihu names Job directly, opening a fresh unit: הַאֲזִ֣ינָה זֹּ֣את אִיּ֑וֹב (‘listen to this, Job’, web:Job.37.14), WEB “Listen to this, Job. Stand still,” (web:Job.37.14). Within this speech's 57 verses, איוב (‘Job’) appears only here (sweep: 1 occurrence across Job.36.1-Job.37.24), matching the book-wide pattern in which Elihu, alone among the interlocutors, addresses Job by name inside speech. An anaphoric refrain follows -- הֲ֭תֵדַע at 37:15 and the byte-identical הֲ֭תֵדַע at 37:16 (‘do you know’, web:Job.37.15-Job.37.16) -- driving a series of rhetorical questions through 37:19-20 that closes on “Will it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?” (web:Job.37.20) before the discourse returns to third-person description at 37:21.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through 37:24 to the speech's end was considered, but 37:21 drops the second-person interrogatives and returns to third-person description, so the interrogative block is kept as its own span.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Direct naming of Job with anaphoric interrogative volley throughout

next_row.boundary_rationale: The narrative formula “Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,” (web:Job.38.1) is the FIRST (sweep: 3 book-wide) of exactly three יְהוָ֣ה-spoken vaya'an tokens in the book, byte-settled in canonical verse order as 38:1, 40:1, 40:6, and it alone carries this part's opening seam against the close of Elihu's fourth speech at 37:24: chapter 38 carries none of the book's 39 Masoretic paragraph marks, so the seam rests on the formula. A petuchah (single-witness) does follow oshb:Job.37.24 — “Therefore men revere him. He doesn't regard any who are wise of heart."” (web:Job.37.24) — on the far side, closing Elihu's speech, but that corroboration belongs to the seam's other edge, not to chapter 38 itself. Inside the formula the ketiv מנ הסערה gives way to the qere מִ֥ן הַסְּעָרָ֗ה 'from the storm' (oshb:Job.38.1), and one paseq (single-witness) segments the verse. Verse 2 opens the direct address with the interrogative מִ֤י זֶ֨ה, “"Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?” (web:Job.38.2 — the phrase mi-zeh recurs once more only, at 42:3 (sweep: 2 book-wide), where Job quotes it back at his retraction, framing an inclusio across the whole interchange), carrying its own paseq (single-witness). Verse 3 opens with the imperative אֱזָר נָ֣א, “gird now,” followed by the gird-up device’s two-word counting core — the comparative כְגֶ֣בֶר (‘like a man’) plus the direct object חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ (‘your loins’) (sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 38:3 and 40:7): אֱזָר נָ֣א כְגֶ֣בֶר חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ וְ֝אֶשְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי – “Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me!” (web:Job.38.3, oshb:Job.38.3), the two-word phrase recurring at 40:7 and nowhere else (sweep: 2 book-wide), opening the second whirlwind speech in an identical parallel gesture.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the frame formula into its own one-verse row was set aside because 38:1's vaya'an and the 2-3 challenge form one uninterrupted address opening the interrogation, not two separable movements.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Yahweh first vaya'an: who darkens counsel, gird up challenge

next_row.boundary_rationale: The cosmos catalog's opening item begins with the interrogative אֵיפֹ֣ה הָ֭יִיתָ, “"Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.” (web:Job.38.4), matched by the chained מִי-questions at verses 5-6 (who determined the earth's measures, who stretched the line, who laid the cornerstone) and closing on the doxological image “when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?” (web:Job.38.7) — בְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים “sons of God” (oshb:Job.38.7) casts creation as a scene the divine court witnessed — an echo, not a verbatim recurrence, of the frame's own court-language register: the frame's phrase is articled, בְּנֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים (skeleton sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 1:6 and 2:1), while 38:7's is anarthrous, בְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים (skeleton sweep: 1 book-wide, 38:7 only) — two distinct string objects bearing the same register. The item ends here because verse 8 turns to a new participant, the sea, rather than repeating the earth's-foundation questions.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A four-verse split at 5|6, isolating the cornerstone image on its own, was rejected: 38:5-6 carry the pronoun-מִי chain (מִי שָׂ֣ם/א֤וֹ מִֽי at 38:5, with 38:6's opening interrogative עַל מָ֭ה (“upon what”) a variant form rather than a break, and 38:6's own מִֽי closing the pair), and 38:7 is a dependent doxological close — not a fourth question — rather than a claim that all three verses run as one uninterrupted chain.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Foundations interrogative with morning stars and divine court scene

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The precipitation cluster opens by repeating verbatim the formula that opened the row above: הֲ֭בָאתָ אֶל אֹצְר֣וֹת שָׁ֑לֶג, “Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,” (web:Job.38.22). Its own near edge sits at the participant/topic shift from the light-and-darkness dwelling-place of the row before this one to snow-and-hail storehouses here; the fresh הֲ-interrogative opener is texture (fifteen such openers fall across 38:16-39:12) rather than the discriminator by itself. Interior turns follow at every new form water takes: אֵי זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יֵחָ֣לֶק, “By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?” (web:Job.38.24) — the same interrogative-adverb-plus-demonstrative device that opened the row before this one at 38:19 (sweep: 2 book-wide, its only two members), recurring here mid-cluster rather than at an edge, disclosed rather than denied; its own two subjects, light and the east wind, are an outlier inside this otherwise water-forms cluster, not a further form of water. מִֽי פִלַּ֣ג לַשֶּׁ֣טֶף תְּעָלָ֑ה, “Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm,” (web:Job.38.25) turns to the flood channel on a fresh verse-initial bare מי, a member the interior-turn list must include alongside הֲיֵשׁ לַמָּטָ֥ר אָ֑ב, “Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?” (web:Job.38.28), and מִבֶּ֣טֶן מִ֭י יָצָ֣א הַקָּ֑רַח, “Whose womb did the ice come out of? Who has given birth to the gray frost of the sky?” (web:Job.38.29), where the same pronoun sits as the verse's second word rather than its opener. The cluster closes on ice and the frozen deep, “The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.” (web:Job.38.30), before verse 31 turns to the constellations with its own fresh הֲ-interrogative.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking this cluster at 27|28 into storehouses-and-channels versus parentage-and-birth was considered and set aside on the ice/frost thematic close that unifies 22-30, but the live rival is the seam at 38:23|38:24: snow and hail reserved for a day of battle, “which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?” (web:Job.38.23), against the turn to the way of light and the east wind at 38:24. That rival carries its own byte-true device — the אֵי זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ repeat shared with 38:19 — which argues for continuity across the seam it sits on rather than a fresh boundary there, since the device's only two members bracket the 38:19|38:24 span rather than opening at 38:24 alone; engaged rather than denied, it does not overturn this row's own edges.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Snow and rain treasuries with weather-distribution disjunctive frame

prev_row.boundary_rationale: Two paired items share a row here. הֲ֭בָאתָ עַד נִבְכֵי יָ֑ם, “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?” (web:Job.38.16), opens the boundaries-of-earth item (16-18), closing with “Have you comprehended the earth in its width? Declare, if you know it all.” (web:Job.38.18). Verse 19 turns to a second interrogative device, the interrogative-adverb-plus-demonstrative construction אֵי זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יִשְׁכָּן, “What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,” (web:Job.38.19) — the identical phrase recurs once more only, at 38:24 (sweep: 2 book-wide), framing a light-motif that spans the row's far side. The pairing closes on the taunt “Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!” (web:Job.38.21) before verse 22 reopens with the same הֲ֭בָאתָ that opened this row. That verbatim repetition — not the mere presence of an interrogative-he opener, which recurs fifteen times across 38:16-39:12 — is what marks the next movement; this row's own unity across its two items rests on the shared theme, the limits of the knowable earth, argued below.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this row at 18|19 into two three-verse rows was set aside because both items share one theme, the limits of the knowable earth, and the second closes with a taunt that answers the boundaries-of-earth question.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Earth boundaries and light-darkness dwelling with paired interrogatives

next_row.boundary_rationale: This row closes the cosmos catalog across two interior turns. הַֽ֭תְקַשֵּׁר מַעֲדַנּ֣וֹת כִּימָ֑ה, “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?” (web:Job.38.31), opens the constellations item on a patah-plus-meteg interrogative-he (not the more common hataf-patah spelling; the same patah-plus-meteg spelling recurs only at its sibling verse inside this row, 38:35 — sweep: 2 within the 38:16-39:12 catalog window; book-wide the spelling occurs in 9 verses (8 interrogative)), running through the heavens' laws at verse 33 (“Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?”, web:Job.38.33). הֲתָרִ֣ים לָעָ֣ב קוֹלֶ֑ךָ, “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover you?” (web:Job.38.34) turns to weather and, at verse 36, to a bare מִי שָׁ֭ת בַּטֻּח֣וֹת חָכְמָ֑ה, “Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?” (web:Job.38.36) — the catalog's turn toward wisdom, a two-verse pair rather than one event: מִֽי יְסַפֵּ֣ר שְׁחָקִ֣ים בְּחָכְמָ֑ה, “Who can count the clouds by wisdom?” (web:Job.38.37), repeats the same bare-מי wisdom opener immediately after. The whole cosmos catalog then closes on the mundane image of dust caking into clods (“when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?”, web:Job.38.38), before verse 39 opens the animal catalog with a fresh interrogative aimed at the lioness. The he-interrogative opener recurring across this whole span is texture, not the discriminator by itself: fifteen verses open on it between 38:16 and 39:12, of which five run consecutively inside this row alone (31-35); this row's own edges rest instead on the topic shifts named above — constellations, weather, wisdom, dust.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the cosmos catalog at verse 33 with the constellations, so that 34-38's weather-and-wisdom material would open a fresh row, was considered. No speech or scene marker separates 38:33 from 38:34 — but by that same test no speech or scene marker separates 38:30 from 38:31 or 38:38 from 38:39 either, so the criterion cannot be what distinguishes this row's own edges from the rejected seam; the ground here is instead the topic continuity of 31-38 as one movement through the sky's phenomena, closing on dust before the animal catalog's fresh subject at 39.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Hail treasury reserved for day of conflict and judgment

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The Behemoth poem opens on the full creature-introduction phrase, oshb:Job.40.15 “הִנֵּה נָ֣א בְ֭הֵמוֹת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֣יתִי עִמָּ֑ךְ חָ֝צִ֗יר כַּבָּקָ֥ר יֹאכֵֽל”, web:Job.40.15 “See now behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.” — the presentative הִנֵּה נָ֣א plus the named creature בְ֭הֵמוֹת plus the אֲשֶׁר-relative clause together, not the bare presentative particle alone: הִנֵּה נָ֣א itself recurs verse-initially inside this row's own span, at 40:16 (הִנֵּה נָ֣א כֹח֣וֹ בְמָתְנָ֑יו וְ֝אֹנ֗וֹ בִּשְׁרִירֵ֥י בִטְנֽוֹ, “Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.”), and a third presentative-class opening, the hen variant without נא, sits at 40:23 (הֵ֤ן יַעֲשֹׁ֣ק נָ֭הָר לֹ֣א יַחְפּ֑וֹז יִבְטַ֓ח כִּֽי יָגִ֖יחַ יַרְדֵּ֣ן אֶל פִּֽיהוּ) — both disclosed here rather than passed over, since the bare particle class does not by itself uniquely locate 40:15; the fuller phrase quoted above, with its named creature and relative clause, has no counterpart at either recurrence. בהמות here names the creature, distinct from the same consonant string's common-plural sense (beasts/animals) at oshb:Job.12.7 “וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁאַל נָ֣א בְהֵמ֣וֹת וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וְע֥וֹף הַ֝שָּׁמַ֗יִם וְיַגֶּד לָֽךְ”, web:Job.12.7 “But ask the animals now, and they will teach you; the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.” — a genuine homograph hazard, independently re-derived here: the bare (unprefixed) noun sweeps to 2 book-wide members (12:7 the common plural, 40:15 the creature), a distinct object from the prefixed מבהמות at 35:11, outside this bare count. The poem runs through body description to its theological center, web:Job.40.19 “He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.”, then habitat and security, closing on a capture-challenge question, web:Job.40.24 “Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?”, that sets up the Leviathan capture-challenge opening the next row. No interrogative, vocative, or formula interrupts between 40:15 and 40:24; the poem runs as one continuous description, at the wide end of the strophe guide but not beyond it.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A mood shift reopens the address at web:Job.40.10 “Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.”: the interrogative challenge closing at web:Job.40.9 “Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?”, gives way here to an imperative test series running through web:Job.40.13 “Hide them in the dust together. Bind their faces in the hidden place.”. The verse also opens with an imperative-plus-נא pattern, עֲדֵ֥ה נָ֣א גָֽא֣וֹן וָגֹ֑בַהּ וְה֖וֹד וְהָדָ֣ר תִּלְבָּֽשׁ, matching אֱזָר נָ֣א at 40:7 in grammatical shape though not in verb or object; that shape is ambient rather than discriminating (word-token sweep of imperative-plus-נא: 18 book-wide, after setting aside the four presentative הנה-נא verses and the one negative אל-נא verse), so it is disclosed here as texture rather than claimed as the driver. The narrower two-member device this shape recalls, the gird-up formula's own two-word core כְגֶ֣בֶר חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ (sweep: 2 book-wide, 38:3 and 40:7 only), does not reach 40:10 at all and sits entirely before this row's near edge, so it argues nothing about the 40:9|40:10 seam either way. The strophe closes on the concession this whole re-challenge has been building toward, web:Job.40.14 “Then I will also admit to you that your own right hand can save you.”, immediately before web:Job.40.15 opens the Behemoth poem on the fuller creature-introduction phrase, הִנֵּה נָ֣א בְ֭הֵמוֹת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֣יתִי עִמָּ֑ךְ, “See now behemoth, which I made as well as you.” — a genuine topic shift to a new named creature that closes this row's far edge.

This whole row sits inside the numbering offset zone, disclosed at every original-language cite (mt_v = web_v + 24 for this span). The series of hook, rope, petition, covenant, and traders'-barter questions develops the capture-challenge through its closing imperative, web:Job.41.8 = oshb:Job.40.32 “שִׂים עָלָ֥יו כַּפֶּ֑ךָ זְכֹ֥ר מִ֝לְחָמָ֗ה אַל תּוֹסַֽף”, web:Job.41.8 “Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.”, before the register shifts to a הן-opening declarative at web:Job.41.9. The eight verses are not uniformly 2nd-person, disclosed rather than smoothed over: most carry 2nd-person (2ms) forms addressed to Job (40:25, 40:26, 40:29, 40:31-32), but the petition verse, web:Job.41.3 = oshb:Job.40.27 “הֲיַרְבֶּ֣ה אֵ֭לֶיךָ תַּחֲנוּנִ֑ים אִם יְדַבֵּ֖ר אֵלֶ֣יךָ רַכּֽוֹת”, opens with a 3ms subject verb; its addressee is carried by the twice-repeated prepositional suffix אֵ֭לֶיךָ rather than by the verb, and the traders'-barter verse, web:Job.41.6 = oshb:Job.40.30 “יִכְר֣וּ עָ֭לָיו חַבָּרִ֑ים יֶ֝חֱצ֗וּהוּ בֵּ֣ין כְּֽנַעֲנִֽים”, carries no 2nd-person form of any kind — two of the eight verses depart cleanly from this row's dominant register. The covenant verse, web:Job.41.4 = oshb:Job.40.28 “הֲיִכְרֹ֣ת בְּרִ֣ית עִמָּ֑ךְ תִּ֝קָּחֶ֗נּוּ לְעֶ֣בֶד עוֹלָֽם”, is a third, less settled case: its opening colon likewise opens 3ms with the addressee carried by the prepositional suffix עִמָּ֑ךְ rather than by the verb, but its second colon's verb תִּ֝קָּחֶ֗נּוּ is a taw-prefix form its own WEB witness reads as 2nd person (“you should take him”); no morph layer on disk can exclude a 3fs parse, so 40:28's register is disclosed as mixed rather than counted flatly with the other two.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the WEB 40|41 chapter division as the driver for this row's near edge was rejected because that division is tier-4 metadata; the seam instead rests on the fresh 2nd-person capture-address opening at 41:1, argued from the creature-introduction syntax with the offset disclosed.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The narrator's voice opens the prose epilogue with an explicit temporal-causal transition, oshb:Job.42.7 “וַיְהִ֗י אַחַ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֶל אִיּ֑וֹב וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל אֱלִיפַ֣ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֗י חָרָ֨ה אַפִּ֤י בְךָ֙ וּבִשְׁנֵ֣י רֵעֶ֔יךָ כִּ֠י לֹ֣א דִבַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֛י נְכוֹנָ֖ה כְּעַבְדִּ֥י אִיּֽוֹב”, web:Job.42.7 “It was so, that after Yahweh had spoken these words to Job, Yahweh said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.”, immediately after the petuchah (single-witness) following the poetry's close. YHWH's verdict speech to Eliphaz names all three friends' failure and closes with a refrain, repeated verbatim at the end of the following verse, “for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has” (web:Job.42.7, web:Job.42.8), a doubled formula binding the two verses of direct speech into one unit. The scene closes with the narrator's report of compliance and acceptance, web:Job.42.9 “So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what Yahweh commanded them, and Yahweh accepted Job.”, before the topic shifts from the friends' obedience to Job's own restored fortune in the next row.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting YHWH's direct speech from the friends' compliance report into two rows was rejected because the doubled refrain closing both verses of that speech binds the verdict scene into one unit, and the compliance report completes that same scene rather than opening a new one.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Verdict scene: Yahweh rebukes friends, demands sacrifice and intercession

prev_row.boundary_rationale: An imperative opens this strophe at 42:4, oshb:Job.42.4 “שְֽׁמַֽע נָ֭א וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר אֶ֝שְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי”, web:Job.42.4 “You said, 'Listen, now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.'”, echoing not YHWH's opening challenge (quoted in the row before this one) but the question-and-answer commissioning clause shared with both whirlwind speeches: אֶ֝שְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי is byte-identical to the same clause closing oshb:Job.40.7 (sweep: 2 book-wide at that exact pointed clause), and matches the clause closing oshb:Job.38.3 only as a prefix-stripped substring at the accent_stripped/skeleton tiers, since 38:3's form carries a prefixed conjunctive vav (וְ֝אֶשְׁאָלְךָ֗) that the 40:7 and 42:4 forms both lack — two objects, not one, disclosed here rather than claimed as a three-way exact match (a bare-spelling skeleton count of 3 is a substring artifact of the prefixed 38:3 form, not a third independent byte-identical member). The 'You said' attribution at web:Job.42.4 is a WEB translational supplement: the Hebrew carries no quotative verb of saying that attributes the words to a speaker — its own verb of speech, אֲדַבֵּ֑ר, is Job's 1cs 'and I will speak', not an amar-form — and the formula-spine inventory has no member at 42:3 or 42:4. The retraction turns from recollection to transformed perception, web:Job.42.5 “I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.”, and closes on the confession of repentance, oshb:Job.42.6 “עַל כֵּ֭ן אֶמְאַ֣ס וְנִחַ֑מְתִּי עַל עָפָ֥ר וָאֵֽפֶר”, web:Job.42.6 “Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”. A rival seam is disclosed rather than adopted: the ve'attah turn stands mid-verse at 42:5 (word 4 of 6, opening the second colon, וְ֝עַתָּ֗ה), the sole verse-medial member of an eight-member book-wide skeleton sweep (6:28, 30:1, 30:9, 30:16, 35:15, 37:21, 42:5, 42:8) whose other seven members are verse-initial; six of those seven elsewhere mark poetic strophe turns, and the seventh, 42:8, sits in the prose epilogue; the two-strophe grain of 42:1-6 (this row and the one before it) stays defensible on the mi-zeh inclusio (38:2/42:3, bracketing the whole whirlwind exchange, not only this row's material) and the commissioning-clause echo closing this row's own opening verse, without relying on a WEB-supplied quotation-frame warrant. A petuchah follows this verse (single-witness), corroborating this row's far edge, where the discourse shifts to the prose narrator's voice.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating the hearing/seeing verse as its own row was rejected because no intervening formula, vocative, or interrogative opens 42:5: the imperative-plus-commissioning-clause quotation that opens this row closes at the end of 42:4, and the transformed-perception statement of 42:5 follows immediately within the same strophe rather than opening a fresh one.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Job echoes gird-up commissioning then retracts prior words

next_row.boundary_rationale: The topic turns from the friends' compliance to Job's own restoration, oshb:Job.42.10 “וַֽיהוָ֗ה שָׁ֚ב אֶת שבית שְׁב֣וּת אִיּ֔וֹב בְּהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֖וֹ בְּעַ֣ד רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַ֧יֹּסֶף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאִיּ֖וֹב לְמִשְׁנֶֽה”, web:Job.42.10 “Yahweh restored Job's prosperity when he prayed for his friends. Yahweh gave Job twice as much as he had before.” (the OSHB extract carries a ketiv/qere pair here, שבית against שבות, disclosed rather than glossed over: the ketiv's medial yod and the qere's medial vav disagree on precisely which root the noun belongs to — shin-bet-he or shin-vav-bet — so the pair leaves the noun's root open rather than confirming a doubled root; what the verse does show is a consonantal echo, texture-tier, between the perfect שָׁ֚ב and the noun itself, marking the scene's opening). The scene continues with the family and acquaintance reunion, comfort, and gift-giving through web:Job.42.11 “Then all his brothers, all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, came to him and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that Yahweh had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money, and everyone a ring of gold.”. A samekh follows this verse (single-witness); the next verse turns from social restoration to a formal, itemized count of possessions, marking this row's far edge.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating the restoration statement from the family reunion into two rows was rejected because both develop the same social/relational restoration before the itemized possessions count begins in the next row.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Restoration scene: fortune restored and family returns to Job
